sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Whitehall Township?
sections.html:
Whitehall is a home rule township in Lehigh County, so the rules that matter most to a seller come from the township building on MacArthur Road, not from a city hall. The big one is a mandatory resale inspection, and it shapes how fast a sale can close.

The township covers about 12.6 square miles on the north side of Allentown, with the Lehigh River marking its eastern edge. The Census Bureau estimates 29,405 residents for July 2025, a gain of 0.8 percent over the 2020 base. Roughly 62 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 sits at $262,100. Households count 11,664, with a median household income of $75,658.

Local history explains the housing stock. Farming and then the Lehigh Canal, iron furnaces and the "Cement Belt" built villages such as Hokendauqua, Cementon, Fullerton and Egypt, and after World War II the township became an Allentown suburb. The villages merged under a single Whitehall post office identity in 1968, and voters adopted the home rule charter in 1974.

sections.h2: Does Whitehall Township require an inspection before I sell?
sections.html:
Yes. The township's FAQ says it requires an inspection for the resale of your property, and its permits page adds that a change of use or occupancy, including a home sale, needs a certificate of occupancy.

The township says each time a property is offered for sale or lease it needs a fresh inspection and a new certificate, even when a rental has several tenants in a year. Its Certificate of Occupancy Application and Guide lays out the steps:

  • Submit the inspection request form with the fee to the Bureau of Development at 3219 MacArthur Road.
  • An inspector contacts you within 1 to 3 business days, and the visit is set within 5 to 10 business days.
  • If nothing is wrong, the clear certificate is issued within 1 to 3 business days.
  • Payment is by cash, check or money order only. The form says cards are not accepted.

Add those windows up and the paperwork alone can take two to three weeks, so ask for the inspection as soon as you pick a settlement date.

sections.h2: What does the Whitehall inspection cost, and what do inspectors check?
sections.html:
Whitehall Township charges listed on the township inspection form (revised May 2023) and FAQ page
ItemCharge
Single-family resale inspection$65
Apartment unit inspection$35 per unit
Conditional certificate for an as-is single-family sale$65 plus a $100 deposit
Conditional certificate for a rental of up to five units$100 plus a $250 deposit
Moving permit$5

Call the township at 610-437-5524 to confirm amounts before you mail a check, since the form carries a 2023 revision date.

The township calls the visit a targeted safety inspection, not a full home inspection. Items on its checklist include working smoke detectors on every level and in each sleeping area, a carbon monoxide alarm near bedrooms where a fireplace, attached garage or fuel-burning heater exists, GFCI outlets in kitchens, baths and laundry areas, handrails on stairs of four or more risers, a 100-amp minimum electrical service, a concrete basement floor and visible house numbers at least four inches tall. Missing items are the usual reason for a failed first pass.

sections.h2: What happens if the inspection finds problems?
sections.html:
You have two paths. Fix the violations and have the inspector return, or sell as is with a conditional certificate. The guide says repairs must be corrected and reinspected within 30 days or before settlement.

For an as-is sale, the seller gives the inspection report to the other party, and a notarized Buyer or Seller Acceptance Form goes back to the township with the added fees. The conditional certificate allows the transfer only. Nobody can move in until all required repairs pass inspection, and the deposit comes back once a clear certificate is issued inside the allotted time.

This matters for homes that need work. Heirs, landlords and owners with deferred repairs often cannot finish a punch list before closing, which is why buyers who purchase as is tend to pair well with the conditional certificate route. Ask any buyer, cash or financed, who will sign the acceptance form and who will complete the repairs.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording steps apply in Lehigh County?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania charges a realty transfer tax of 1 percent of the value, and the Department of Revenue says both grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable. County recorders usually collect it alongside any local transfer tax, so the deed cannot be recorded until the tax is paid.

  • The Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds sits at the courthouse, 455 W. Hamilton Street, Room 122, in Allentown, open 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Monday to Friday. The phone is 610-782-3162.
  • Transfers between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings are generally exempt, and a family exemption has to be stated on the deed.
  • A Statement of Value (REV-183) accompanies any transfer that does not pay the full tax, does not state full consideration or claims an exemption.

Ask the Recorder or your closing agent for the local rate that applies to a Whitehall address, because the municipal and school district share is set locally.

sections.h2: How do rental properties change a Whitehall sale?
sections.html:
Landlords face one extra rule. The township requires every non-owner-occupied property to name a local responsible agent whose office or home is within 10 miles of the township boundary. That person must be reachable in an emergency and authorized to accept legal service for the owner.

The inspection request form asks whether the property will be a rental and, if so, for the agent's name, address, daytime and after-hours phone numbers. Tenants who leave before closing also trigger paperwork, because the township asks for a moving permit when anyone moves into, out of or within the township. The FAQ prices that permit at $5 and says it is issued at the Township Tax Office from 8:00am to 4:00pm.

An owner with a tenant in place can still sell, but the inspector needs access to every room, attic and the exterior, so plan notice to the tenant early.

sections.h2: How do schools and neighborhoods affect resale in Whitehall?
sections.html:
Buyers looking at Whitehall compare it with other Lehigh Valley suburbs, and the Whitehall-Coplay School District is the main draw. It serves the township and neighboring Coplay, and ninth through twelfth graders attend Whitehall High School. Several parochial and private schools sit inside the township too, including Good Shepherd Catholic School, Lehigh Valley Lutheran School and St. Elizabeth Regional School.

Shopping and commuting add appeal. The Lehigh Valley Mall is the largest shopping mall based in the Lehigh Valley, and MacArthur Road (PA 145) carries retail traffic past an interchange with US 22, the Lehigh Valley Thruway. PA 329 crosses the northern part of the township, and LANta buses serve the MacArthur Road corridor. As of 2018 the township maintained about 97.6 miles of its own roads, with PennDOT handling roughly 23 miles.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Whitehall house without a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: No. Whitehall Township requires an inspection and a certificate of occupancy for a resale, and the new owner cannot occupy the property until one is issued. A conditional certificate is available for as-is sales.

faqs.q: How much is the Whitehall resale inspection?
faqs.a: The township's form lists $65 for a single-family home and $35 per apartment unit. An as-is sale adds a $100 deposit for a house, per the form revised in May 2023, so confirm the current amount with the township.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Whitehall house as is if it fails inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller or buyer signs a notarized acceptance form, pays the added fees and receives a conditional certificate that allows the sale only. All listed repairs must pass inspection before anyone occupies the home.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Whitehall home sale?
faqs.a: The state says buyer and seller are both liable for the 1 percent state tax, and the contract decides how the cost is split. The deed is not recorded until the tax is paid, so your closing agent usually collects it at settlement.

faqs.q: Do I need a local agent if my Whitehall house is a rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Non-owner-occupied properties must have a responsible agent within 10 miles of the township. The inspection request form asks for that person's contact details whenever the property is a rental.
